sections.html:
Birmingham is the seat of Jefferson County in north central Alabama, with parts of the city reaching into Shelby County. The metro area holds more than 1.19 million people, and the city itself had an estimated 196,357 in 2024. The population peaked at 340,887 in 1960 and stood at 200,733 in 2020, a drop of about 41 percent as residents moved to suburbs such as Hoover, Vestavia Hills, Alabaster and Gardendale. Sellers inside the city should expect buyers to compare their street with those suburbs, so be ready to explain what your neighborhood offers.

That history is why Birmingham properties vary so much by neighborhood. Growth moved to the suburbs after 1960, so one address can mean a very different house, lot and street from the next.

sections.h2: Neighborhoods and how to describe yours
sections.html:
The city covers about 149.54 square miles and is divided into 23 communities and 99 neighborhoods. Each neighborhood has an association that is consulted on zoning changes and other local matters. Buyers search by community, so name yours in any listing or offer request.

Birmingham sits in Jones Valley between long parallel ridges at the tail end of the Appalachians. Red Mountain lies just south of downtown. The area called Over the Mountain, which includes Mountain Brook, Vestavia Hills, Homewood and Hoover, was largely shielded from the smoke of the industrial city,. A house on a ridge, in the valley or on a slope has different drainage, access and views, and a buyer will notice. Mention any steep driveway, retaining wall or runoff problem so the buyer hears it from you first.

Birmingham sits in the part of the South that gets frequent tornadoes, often called Dixie Alley. The greater area was hit by two F5 tornadoes, in 1977 and 1998, and by an EF4 tornado in the April 2011 outbreak.

  • Spring and November bring strong to severe thunderstorms.
  • Highs reach 90 degrees on about 65 days a year.
  • Late summer and fall can bring tropical storm effects from the Gulf.

Roofs, mature trees and old drainage are worth a look before any sale, and a buyer's inspector will ask about all three. Keep storm repair receipts and any insurance claim letters where you can find them.

sections.h2: Code notices and which county holds your deed
sections.html:
The city has a strong-mayor government with a mayor and a nine-member council, which replaced the old city commission in 1962. If your house is vacant or damaged, ask the city about any open code notice before you list or accept an offer. An unresolved notice can slow a closing and may affect what a buyer will pay.

Because the city reaches into both Jefferson and Shelby counties, confirm which county holds your parcel. The two counties keep separate records, and a Birmingham mailing address does not always show which county handles the deed. A closing agent can check this in a few minutes.

A Birmingham deed is recorded with the probate judge of the county where the land sits. The state recording tax is 50 cents per $500 of value or fraction of that. The deed must come with proof of the actual price paid, and a mortgage that paid its own tax is taken out of the taxable value first.

Property tax is due October 1 and delinquent after December 31, so check the bill's status before you sign anything.

Before you ask for offers, work through these questions:

  • Who is on the deed, and has anyone died or divorced since it was recorded?
  • Are there open liens, back taxes or code violations on the address?
  • Are tenants in the house, and what does the lease say?
  • Which county holds the parcel?
  • What repairs do you already know about, and do you have receipts for past work?

The closing agent runs the title search, yet you save days by knowing the answers beforehand. A surprise discovered late costs more time than one discovered early. A problem on this list does not end the sale. It simply has to be fixed or priced in before the deed changes hands.

sections.h2: When a cash sale makes sense
sections.html:
Cash works best when speed, condition or paperwork outweigh the wait for a listing price. In a large, varied city, the usual cases include inherited houses, rentals with difficult tenants, deferred repairs and owners relocating for a job.

We buy houses in Birmingham as-is, with no commission and no closing costs on your side, and you can decline any offer. Compare it with a listing plan, a local agent's price opinion and your own timeline.

Think about what a listing would really involve for your house. Repairs come first, then photos and showings, then a buyer's inspection and a lender's appraisal, and each step has a way of reopening the price. A cash offer cuts that chain short and fixes the closing date, but a retail buyer may pay more for a house in good shape. Neither route is right for everyone, which is why a written offer is worth getting before you decide.

An empty house brings its own risks. Insurers often limit coverage on vacant property, neighbors notice overgrown yards, and a broken window or a leak can turn a small repair into a large one. If you are living elsewhere while the house waits, ask your insurer what rules apply to vacancy and visit often enough to catch problems early.

Open code notices deserve prompt attention. Call the city, learn exactly what the notice requires and note any deadline written on it. Sellers sometimes assume a notice has to be cleared before an offer, but a buyer can price the work in, provided the closing agent sees the notice and the title search is clean. Hiding it is the one thing that never works, because it surfaces during closing and can sink the sale at the last moment.

On the closing date, the closing agent presents a settlement statement showing the price, the payoff of any mortgage, the tax balance, the recording tax and any other charges. You review it, sign the deed and any other papers, and the deed is recorded with the probate judge. Proceeds go to you after liens and taxes are paid. Ask for the statement ahead of time so the numbers hold no surprises.

If you are moving out, plan to leave the house empty, hand over keys and arrange final utility readings. If tenants are in place, your closing agent will explain how deposits and rent are handled so nothing is missed.

faqs.q: What county is Birmingham, Alabama, in?
faqs.a: Birmingham is the county seat of Jefferson County, and parts of the city extend into Shelby County. Confirm which county your parcel is in before you record a deed.

faqs.q: How many people live in Birmingham, Alabama?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 200,733 residents, and the 2024 estimate is 196,357. The metro area holds more than 1.19 million people.

faqs.q: How much is the recording tax on a Birmingham house sale?
faqs.a: Alabama charges 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500 conveyed, after subtracting a mortgage that already paid its own tax. The probate judge calculates the amount when the deed is filed.

faqs.q: When is the Alabama property tax deadline?
faqs.a: Taxes are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. Check the bill's status before you sign.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Birmingham house with tenants or code issues?
faqs.a: Yes. Houses are sold as-is with tenants and with open repairs all the time. Have the leases and any city notices ready, because they affect both the price and the closing.
